hyps.why: At tiny learning rates (1e-5 to 1.3e-4) training is badly under-converged after 243 epochs, so raising the rate gives large gains, while at mid/high rates it gives little or even harms.
Rates of 0.0774 and above already make Adam unstable, so pushing them higher causes divergence or dead ReLUs and sharp accuracy drops.
Lowering an unstable high rate restores convergence, giving much larger benefits than lowering an already moderate or low rate.
Larger batches reduce gradient noise and the number of updates, which damps the instability of high learning rates instead of slowing useful training.
With a low learning rate, larger batches mean fewer optimizer steps in a fixed epoch budget, worsening under-training.
Smaller batches give more updates per epoch, which matters most when a small step size leaves the model under-converged.
Large batches get few steps and low gradient noise, so they both need and tolerate larger learning rates.
Below about 1e-3 the L2 penalty is negligible, but at 0.0167 to 1 further increases strongly underfit the network and reduce accuracy.
Very narrow networks (16 to 40 units) are capacity-limited, so widening helps them far more than it helps already wide networks with saturated capacity.
Deeper ReLU stacks are more prone to exploding activations and dead units under very large learning rates, so adding layers hurts more there.
